step1.text:
Orthogonal (Scrape Creators LinkedIn profile): Read a public LinkedIn person profile by its URL: name, location, about, experience with dates, education, follower count and recent posts. Sync. Use when a linkedin.com/in/ URL is already known.
Price: $0.02 per call, paid by this machine's wallet straight to the provider.
Request: GET https://x402.orthogonal.com/scrapecreators/v1/linkedin/profile
Inputs:
- url (string, required); Public LinkedIn profile URL, https://www.linkedin.com/in/<handle>; min length 1
Example input: {"url":"https://www.linkedin.com/in/person-l"}
Returns: JSON {name, location, followers, about, experience[], education[], recentPosts[]}: the public profile, plus credit counters
To run it, call request({id: "00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000006", input: {...}}) with the inputs above. Nothing has been paid.

result.name: Person L
result.about: Leads a software company and writes about building products.

recentPosts.title: A short post about shipping a product release.

observed: The profile has no job titles: each `experience[]` entry is an organisation with `name`, `url`, sometimes `location`, and `member.startDate` (and `endDate` when ended); there is no title or description field. `startDate` is a string ("2014-02") in one entry and a number (2018) in another. `education[]` mixes board and advisory seats (`@type` "Organization") with schools (`@type` "EducationalOrganization"); only the second kind is education. There is no headline and no skills field, as the spec said. So a LinkedIn read gives the name, place, about text and employers with dates, but not the roles: the skill must still confirm the target role (with its guess as the default) and should ask for a resume file or text when the profile is too thin to fill forms. The skill never opens the LinkedIn URL itself.
